title: Lenin's Revolution and Civil War
welcome_lead: From the Winter Palace storming to NEP: Bolshevik power consolidates.
meta_desc: A-Level history adventure on the 1917 revolutions, Russian Civil War and Lenin's policies.
final_note: You have steered Russia from Romanov to Bolshevik.

concepts.def: Bolshevik seizure of Petrograd on 25 October 1917 (Julian; 7 November Gregorian) led by Lenin and Trotsky.
First Bolshevik decree of 26 October 1917 abolishing private property in land in favour of peasant control.
Punitive peace with Germany signed on 3 March 1918, ceding the Baltics, Ukraine and a quarter of Russia's population.
1918-21 policies of grain requisitioning, nationalisation and labour militarisation to sustain the Civil War.
Bolshevik secret police created on 20 December 1917 under Dzerzhinsky; conducted the Red Terror.
New Economic Policy from March 1921 reintroducing limited private trade and a tax in kind on peasants.

walkthroughs.h2: Why did the Bolsheviks succeed in October?
walkthroughs.body_html: The Provisional Government's failure to deliver land, peace or bread alienated workers and soldiers. Lenin's April Theses demanded 'all power to the Soviets'. The Kornilov affair in August 1917 discredited Kerensky and rearmed the Bolshevik Red Guards. With Bolshevik majorities in Petrograd and Moscow Soviets by September, Trotsky's Military Revolutionary Committee seized key points on 24-25 October with minimal resistance.

Whites, Greens and foreign interventionists challenged Bolshevik control. Trotsky organised the 5-million-strong Red Army with conscripted Tsarist officers monitored by commissars. War Communism extracted grain through Cheka detachments. Famine in 1921 killed 5 million. Victories at Petrograd (October 1919) and Crimea (November 1920) secured Bolshevik power, though Polish defeat at Warsaw August 1920 ended westward expansion.

The Kronstadt sailors' revolt in March 1921 demanding 'soviets without communists' was crushed but prompted policy change. At the Tenth Party Congress Lenin introduced NEP: requisitioning replaced by tax in kind, small businesses denationalised. By 1926 agricultural output regained pre-war levels. NEP also banned factions inside the party, centralising power for later struggles after Lenin's death in January 1924.

options: 3 March 1918
25 October 1917
20 December 1917
7 November 1917

mcqs.q: What replaced War Communism in March 1921?
options: NEP
Five-Year Plan
Collectivisation
Cheka rule

mcqs.q: What did Lenin's April Theses demand in 1917?
options: No support for the Provisional Government, all power to the Soviets, end the war, redistribute land — slogans summarised as 'Peace, Bread, Land'.
The Provisional Government fell because the Tsar returned and reclaimed his throne.
The April Theses created the Soviet Union.
Lenin's April Theses called for an immediate alliance with the Provisional Government.

mcqs.q: Why did Lenin introduce the NEP in 1921?
options: War Communism had collapsed the economy and provoked the Kronstadt revolt; the NEP allowed limited private trade to restore production and stabilise Bolshevik rule.
The NEP was introduced by Stalin to fund the Five-Year Plans.
The Provisional Government fell because the Tsar returned and reclaimed his throne.
The NEP was Lenin's plan to permanently switch Russia to capitalism.

mcqs.q: Why did the Provisional Government fail in 1917?
options: The Provisional Government fell because Lenin was personally more charismatic than Kerensky.
It continued the unpopular war, did not redistribute land, shared 'dual power' with the Petrograd Soviet, and was discredited by the Kornilov affair before the Bolshevik takeover.
The Provisional Government fell because the Tsar returned and reclaimed his throne.
The April Theses created the Soviet Union.
